goal: Build original modules for Circuit Sprint 3D, a playable 3D overhead arcade racer. Each worker writes one focused ES module. Return only source code, with no explanation or Markdown fence.

tasks.objective: Write all of src/track-math.js. Generate a smooth original closed circuit centerline and a nearest-point query. Keep the module concise.
interfaces: Export makeTrackSamples(count = 240), returning count ordered plain {x,z} points around a closed loop. XZ is the horizontal plane; direction is increasing index.
Export nearestTrackPoint(samples, x, z), returning {x,z,tangentX,tangentZ,distance,progress,index}. Tangent is unit forward, distance nonnegative, progress in [0,1), index integer.
No imports or Three.js. Inputs are finite numbers, samples has at least 3 points.
acceptance_checks: Original smooth loop with no self intersection and enough bends to race; count points exactly.
Nearest-point results remain finite at every sample and at the center of the map.
No external assets, DOM, network or extra exports. Raw valid ES module code only.
tasks.context: The renderer will turn these points into a road ribbon. Cars use tangent and progress for steering and lap scoring. A simple deformed oval is sufficient; correctness and legibility matter more than decorative code.

tasks.objective: Write all of src/car-mesh.js. Build a compact original low-poly 3D racing-car mesh with a clear front direction.
interfaces: Import * as THREE from 'three'. Export createCarMesh(color) returning a THREE.Group.
The group origin is car center on the ground. Car forward is local +Z; Y is up. Width around 1.5, length around 2.5, height below 1.2 world units.
The caller moves and rotates the returned group; do not implement physics or input.
acceptance_checks: Procedural body, cockpit, four wheels, and contrasting front accent use only Three.js built-in geometry/materials.
Distinct passed colors are visible; group can be reused for player and AI cars.
No DOM, network, textures or external assets. Raw valid ES module code only.
tasks.context: Game is viewed by a tilted overhead camera, so the silhouette and front direction must read at a small size. Keep geometry construction concise and avoid per-frame work.

tasks.objective: Write all of src/controls.js. Implement reliable keyboard controls for one or two local players.
interfaces: Export createControls(target = window). It installs keydown/keyup listeners and returns { read, dispose }.

read(playerNumber) returns { throttle, brake, steer } with throttle/brake 0 or 1 and steer -1, 0, or 1. Player 1: W or ArrowUp throttle, S or ArrowDown brake, A or ArrowLeft steer left, D or ArrowRight steer right. Player 2: I throttle, K brake, J left, L right.
dispose() removes listeners. Browser window is available; no Three.js dependency.
acceptance_checks: Key state clears on keyup and window blur; repeated keydown does not accumulate state.
Prevent browser scrolling for arrow keys and space only while controls are active.
Both player mappings work at the same time, and dispose is safe to call twice. Raw valid ES module code only.
tasks.context: The game loop polls read(1) and optionally read(2) once per frame. Use event.code so keyboard layout changes do not alter controls. Do not create visible UI or a game loop.
